6a2ad70638d6620013badaef.tagline: An 18th-century manor kept in one family for three centuries — seven suites, saltwater pool, the Minho at the gate.
6a2ad70638d6620013badaef.description:
Carcavelos Manor House has belonged to the same family since the eighteenth century, and the restoration finished in 2025 kept its word: the coffered ceilings are original, the period furniture stayed, and the bathrooms quietly joined this century.

Seven suites open onto six thousand square metres of walled gardens with a saltwater pool. Braga is fifteen minutes away; the Peneda-Gerês National Park begins almost at the gate. Vila Verde around you is working Minho countryside — vines, granite, church bells.

Mornings here are slow by design. Coffee on the terrace, a swim before the sun gets serious, and the day decided over breakfast rather than in advance.

For family gatherings and groups of up to fourteen who want history they can actually live in — with our local team handling everything from arrival to the last espresso.

696533466d209c001510ecfe.tagline: A five-suite villa with heated pool and ocean light, two kilometres from the beach below Montedor lighthouse.
696533466d209c001510ecfe.description:
Eben Lodge sits in a quiet residential corner of Carreço with the Atlantic filling the horizon. Five bedrooms, five bathrooms, a heated private pool, a pool table, and a fireplace for the evenings when the sea air turns crisp.

The beach and the nineteenth-century Montedor lighthouse are under two kilometres away; Viana do Castelo's restaurants, ten minutes. This is the stretch of coast the north keeps for itself — pines, dunes, and surf without crowds.

Days organise themselves: pool until the light softens, a walk to the lighthouse before dinner, grilled fish somewhere the GPS mispronounces.

For up to ten guests — families and groups who want the ocean close and everything else taken care of by our team down the road.

69e7350685a8b000124854c5.tagline: Minimalist architecture and a heated granite infinity pool among the Alvarinho vineyards of the Tâmega valley.
69e7350685a8b000124854c5.description:
Alvarinho Villa stands among the vineyards that name it, in the green hills above Amarante. The architecture is deliberately spare — clean lines, stone, glass — so the valley does the decorating.

Five en-suite bedrooms, air conditioning throughout, and a heated granite infinity pool that holds the last light of the day. The barbecue and gardens face the vines.

The region rewards the curious: Amarante's bridge and pastries, quintas pouring the wine grown around you, the Tâmega for morning walks. Porto is close enough for lunch and far enough to forget.

For up to ten guests who measure luxury in silence, architecture and a very good glass of white — with our concierge arranging tastings, chefs and everything between.

696533722def930014e914e2.tagline: A Minho quinta with tennis court, gym and pool — five bedrooms of light, granite and room to celebrate.
696533722def930014e914e2.description:
Quinta Refúgio Abreu is the kind of Minho house that was built for gatherings: high ceilings, generous reception rooms, and daylight that moves through the house all afternoon.

Five bedrooms sleep ten. Outside there is a pool, a tennis court, a gym and a barbecue under the trees; inside, a fireplace for the shoulder seasons and furniture chosen to be used, not admired.

Delães sits between Braga and Guimarães — Portugal's birthplace on one side, its baroque heart on the other, and the coast under an hour away.

For families and groups who want their own court, their own kitchen garden calm, and a team that sets the stage then disappears until called.

69c415ceab80a8001247452c.tagline: Four restored stone houses and a 300-year-old watermill on the River Coura — with a private river beach.
69c415ceab80a8001247452c.description:
The watermill has stood on the Coura for three hundred years; the four stone houses around it were restored to keep every wall that mattered. Together they sleep twenty across nine bedrooms — one estate, one long table, one river.

The private river beach is the property's quiet superpower: safe, clear water metres from the door, the only access being yours. Air conditioning, fireplaces and board games cover the seasons; the barbecue covers the evenings.

Vilar de Mouros — home of Portugal's oldest music festival — is the village; Caminha is five kilometres, the Atlantic ten.

For family reunions, retreats and celebrations that need history, water and space to spread out — run end to end by our team.

6965335cbf04fe00137431cb.tagline: Two houses, one estate above the Lima — eight bedrooms, infinity pool, sixteen people, one shared memory.
6965335cbf04fe00137431cb.description:
Lima River Houses is two retreats sharing one hillside above the river — bookable whole, as here, for sixteen guests across eight bedrooms and nine bathrooms.

The infinity pool fronts the valley; fireplaces anchor the evenings; the barbecue and gardens absorb long afternoons. Each house keeps its own rhythm — one for the early risers, one for the night owls — while the estate keeps everyone together.

Viana do Castelo and the Atlantic beaches are minutes away; the Lima valley behind you is vinho verde country, all green terraces and Roman bridges.

For big families and groups of friends who want togetherness with escape hatches — and a concierge who has already thought of dinner.

69c567ad7f6873000e9a3c37.tagline: A working-quiet monte in the Alentejo plains — four bedrooms, heated pool, and horizons with nothing to declare.
69c567ad7f6873000e9a3c37.description:
Monte do Sossego means what it says: the hill of quiet. A traditional Alentejo farmhouse — whitewashed, low, honest — with four bedrooms, a heated pool, and a dark-wood rural kitchen made for slow cooking.

The plains around run reddish-gold to the horizon. There is an EV charger, a fireplace for winter stays, unlimited green space, and total privacy — the nearest neighbour is scenery.

Monsaraz, its castle and its wine are thirty kilometres away; the wild trails start at the gate. Nights here are for the barbecue and a sky with actual stars.

For families and groups of up to ten seeking the authentic rural Alentejo — comfort included, hurry excluded.

696533abf142270014026fa9.tagline: A contemporary architectural villa in the hills of Fafe — pool, gardens, and interiors that earn the view.
696533abf142270014026fa9.description:
Stars View is architecture first: a contemporary villa drawn in clean horizontal lines, set in the green hills of Fafe where the Minho begins to climb.

Four bedrooms sleep seven. The private pool and expansive gardens carry the day; the fireplace and refined interiors carry the evening. Air conditioning throughout, barbecue outside, and views that explain the name after dark.

Guimarães — where Portugal was born — is half an hour; Porto just over an hour; the trails and river beaches of the interior Minho start nearby.

For couples and small groups who notice materials, light and silence — and want a design stay without a design-hotel lobby.

69653354109993001383ef5f.tagline: A hilltop estate above the Atlantic — infinity pool, outdoor jacuzzi and seven bedrooms within sound of the waves.
69653354109993001383ef5f.description:
Quinta de Cima holds a private hilltop in Carreço, close enough to the Atlantic that the waves are the house's background music. Seven bedrooms take up to fourteen guests.

The infinity pool looks straight at the sea; the outdoor jacuzzi takes the sunset shift. A games room with billiards, fireplaces, gardens and a barbecue do the rest. Beach essentials are already in the cupboard.

Carreço beach is minutes downhill, Viana do Castelo five kilometres — close for dinner, far enough that the only traffic is gulls.

For families and groups who want the sea view mornings and pool-to-jacuzzi afternoons of a private estate, with our local team on call.

69653335bf04fe0013742743.tagline: Three quiet houses on one green hillside — eight bedrooms, pool and space for sixteen to live at their own pace.
69653335bf04fe0013742743.description:
Nature Hill Duo is a small hillside hamlet of three fully equipped houses outside Viana do Castelo, taken together for groups of up to sixteen.

Modern architecture sits low in the landscape: eight bedrooms in all, a shared pool, gardens, barbecue, EV charger and fireplaces for the cooler months. Each house keeps its own front door — grandparents, friends and teenagers can all have their own address.

The Atlantic beaches and Viana's old town are minutes away; the hill itself offers the silence.

For multi-family holidays and group retreats that want togetherness on their own terms — one booking, three houses, zero logistics, our team handling the rest.

6965330b6d209c001510dd49.tagline: Architect-designed calm above Afife — panoramic sea views, pool, and the best surf beach in town at your feet.
6965330b6d209c001510dd49.description:
Atlantic Lodge was designed by a renowned architecture practice to do one thing perfectly: frame the sea. The interiors stay relaxed and low-key so the panoramic Atlantic views keep the leading role.

Six bedrooms sleep twelve. There is a pool in the garden, a fireplace for misty mornings, board games for slow evenings, and Praia Mariana — the best surf beach in town — a few steps downhill.

Afife is the Minho coast at its wildest: hidden waterfalls and mountain trails inland, white sand and serious waves out front.

For surf houses, family escapes and groups who want the ocean as a housemate — with our concierge handling boards, chefs and everything else.

696533284b583900135ceb91.tagline: A modern villa built for sunsets — heated pool, cinema-sized screen, and the sea filling the balcony.
696533284b583900135ceb91.description:
Sunset Beach Lodge earns its name every single evening: the living room's large balcony faces the Atlantic exactly where the sun goes down.

Four bedrooms sleep up to eleven. The pool is heated, the fireplace is real, the screen is closer to cinema than television, and the beach — essentials provided — is minutes away. Air conditioning and a barbecue complete the kit.

Viana do Castelo delivers the rest: the old town's granite and tiles, the Santa Luzia basilica above it, seafood that was swimming this morning.

For families and groups who plan their days around golden hour — with our team next door for whatever the day needs.

696533d64b583900135d00cc.tagline: A seven-suite manor in the Alto Minho — traditional Portuguese architecture, three floors of considered comfort.
696533d64b583900135d00cc.description:
The Luxury Manor is Alto Minho architecture given room to breathe: a seven-bedroom manor house — every bedroom with its own bathroom — spread over three unhurried floors in Arcos de Valdevez.

Traditional bones carry modern comfort: air conditioning, fireplaces, gardens, and living spaces built for nineteen people without anyone queuing for anything.

From Arcos de Valdevez, Peneda-Gerês opens up: river beaches, granite villages, and some of the greenest country Portugal owns. Ponte de Lima's Tuesday market is a short drive; the coast, under forty minutes.

For large families and celebration weekends that need serious capacity with real character — staffed and provisioned by our team.

6965330729bb8c00141e8cd6.tagline: Where countryside meets sea in Viana — private pool, garden, and beach mornings five minutes from town.
6965330729bb8c00141e8cd6.description:
Habitos Lodge sits in Cafhé, on the soft edge where Viana do Castelo's countryside slides toward the sea. It is a villa for keeping days simple: private pool, real garden, four bedrooms for up to eight guests.

Inside there is air conditioning, a fireplace and board games; outside, a barbecue and beach kit already waiting. Nothing here is complicated, which is the point.

The beaches are minutes away, town five; cycling and horse riding start almost at the door.

For families who want pool mornings, beach afternoons and town-square ice creams in the same day — with our local team a message away.

6965331fec80690013738c68.tagline: A newly renovated design villa with sauna, gym and pool — five minutes from wild Cabedelo beach and Viana's old town.
6965331fec80690013738c68.description:
Villa Aura is the useful kind of luxury: a newly renovated five-bedroom design villa where the sauna, the gym and the outdoor pool are yours alone, wrapped in a tropical garden that hides the world.

Up to twelve guests spread across five bedrooms. Air conditioning, fireplace, board games, EV charger, barbecue — the practical list is long; the atmosphere stays light.

Five minutes one way is Cabedelo, the wild Atlantic beach where the north learns to kitesurf; five minutes the other, Viana do Castelo's historic centre and its restaurants.

For families, friends and slow-living escapes that still want a workout and a sauna — concierge, chefs and transfers included in the thinking.

6a0359b4e343150013abc14d.tagline: A freshly renovated apartment in Darque, calm base for the Minho region
6a0359b4e343150013abc14d.description:
Atlas Hideway is a fully renovated apartment for up to four guests, its open-plan living area done in soft contemporary tones. The kitchen comes equipped with oven, stovetop, dishwasher and coffee machine, and a round dining table sits just off the sofa and smart TV. The master bedroom has a queen bed with hotel-quality linens; the second, a white wooden bunk bed, works well for children. Two bathrooms, both new, include a glass walk-in shower with rainfall head.

The apartment sits in a quiet, residential pocket of Darque, in the Minho region, with cafés, restaurants, grocery stores and pharmacies within a few minutes' walk. The historic centre and waterfront are a short distance away, and from here the wider region opens up on foot, by bike or by car — Atlantic beaches, green hills and stone villages all reachable.

Mornings suit a slow coffee at the dining table before the neighbourhood cafés fill up. Afternoons can go toward the waterfront or a wander through the old centre; evenings return to the sofa, air conditioning on, TV up, dinner cooked in a kitchen that lacks nothing.

It suits families or small groups after a quiet, well-equipped base near Viana do Castelo, with the Portugal Active team on hand throughout the stay.

69dfa9cead7c9c0014cb71c9.tagline: A new house built into the dunes, 200 metres from the Atlantic
69dfa9cead7c9c0014cb71c9.description:
Completed in 2026, Dunes Beach House sits literally within the dunes of Amorosa, in Chafé. White minimalist architecture, anthracite frames and floor-to-ceiling glass bring Atlantic light through every room. Three double bedrooms sleep up to six, two with en-suite bathrooms in large-format porcelain and walk-in showers. Living areas and kitchen open via sliding doors onto the deck and private pool, with the property's own dune rising behind, wildflowers and a timber staircase climbing to a sunset viewpoint over the ocean.

Chafé is a small coastal village between Viana do Castelo and Esposende, the horizon always ocean and the air always salt. Praia da Amorosa, steps away, is one of the most unspoiled stretches of the Minho coast, long sands and high dunes. Viana do Castelo, seven kilometres off, has a historic centre, Cabedelo beach and an early-morning fish market, while coastal trails run through dunes and pine forest toward the green rise of Serra d'Arga.

Mornings mean coffee on the deck before the walk down to Amorosa's clean, unpredictable waves. Evenings call for the timber staircase up the dune, watching the Atlantic take the light before dinner by the pool.

For those wanting genuine coastal remoteness with a proper kitchen and pool close by, the Portugal Active team handles arrival, parking and any local requests.

69653365bf04fe0013743511.tagline: A restored Minho quinta with pool, jacuzzi and garden, ten guests at ease.
69653365bf04fe0013743511.description:
São Julião Retreat pairs a three-bedroom main house with a furnished annex holding a double bedroom, its own bathroom and a sofa-bed lounge, giving four bedrooms and four bathrooms across the estate. Inside, high ceilings and an indoor fireplace sit alongside a fully equipped kitchen and dining table for gathering the group.

The property sits in the countryside near Ponte de Lima, in the Minho region, where green hills roll out toward the mountains and walking and cycling trails thread through the surrounding villages.

Days start on the terrace with coffee and mountain views, and slow down by afternoon at the outdoor pool or the garden loungers. Evenings mean barbecue dinners outside, then the jacuzzi under the stars or the fireplace lit against the Minho chill.

Suited to families or groups of up to ten wanting space and privacy in rural Minho, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

6a7079007df813008d013634.tagline: Seven suites, a private pool and Minho’s mountains, all to yourselves
6a7079007df813008d013634.description:
Seven suites arranged for privacy, each with its own full bathroom and a double bed, plus one additional service bathroom for the group. The kitchen is fully equipped for cooking through a long stay, the dining table set for family meals, and the living room a calm space to gather in the evenings. Upper-floor balconies are furnished for quiet moments outdoors.

The house sits in Vieira do Minho, in the heart of the Minho region, with mountain views from the garden and pool. Traditional restaurants serving the region's classic dishes are just minutes away, and walking routes lead straight into the surrounding countryside.

Days here start slowly, coffee on the balcony with the hills in view, and unfold outdoors, a swim before lunch, a walk through the countryside in the afternoon, dinner at a nearby tasca in the evening. Children have space to run in the garden while the pool stays the day's main draw.

Built for families or groups of up to fourteen travelling together, with pets welcome and cots and high chairs on hand, and backed by Portugal Active's concierge team around the clock.

6a50d66857c8010015595ad0.tagline: A Minho farmhouse retreat with pool, fireside evenings and Ponte de Lima on your doorstep
6a50d66857c8010015595ad0.description:
Agra Country House sits in Arcozelo, just outside Ponte de Lima, with three suites, three bathrooms and space for six. Inside, a fireplace anchors the living areas, alongside a foosball table and games console for slower afternoons, while the fully equipped kitchen and dining table suit both quick breakfasts and long dinners. Outside, the private pool, garden and outdoor dining area make the most of the Minho climate.

Ponte de Lima's centre, reputedly Portugal's oldest town, is 5km away, a ten-minute drive into streets of medieval architecture and regional restaurants. The riverside walkway along the Lima River is close enough for an evening stroll, and local markets and craft shops give a genuine sense of the region.

Mornings suit coffee on the patio before the town wakes up; evenings call for a swim followed by something on the barbecue or fire pit, with the garden turning quiet after dark along its lit path to the door.

Suited to families or small groups after a private, self-contained base in the Minho countryside, with Portugal Active's team on hand for vineyard visits, hiking routes or anything else required.

6965338a753fb0001424acf6.tagline: Two bedrooms on Porto's oldest shopping street, five minutes from the metro
6965338a753fb0001424acf6.description:
Blue Tile Hideaway sits on Rua de Santa Catarina, a two-bedroom, two-bathroom apartment that sleeps up to six with the help of a sofa bed. The kitchen is properly equipped — dishwasher, oven, hob, kettle — and opens onto a bright living area suited to both quiet mornings and family dinners. A crib and high chair are on hand for younger guests.

You're in the middle of Porto's oldest shopping street, close to the Chapel of Souls and its tiled facade, and a short walk from Café Majestic. Bolhão metro station is five minutes on foot, putting the airport and the rest of the city within easy reach.

Mornings start with coffee at the kitchen table before the street outside fills with shoppers and trams. By evening, the walk to Café Majestic or one of the neighbourhood's small restaurants is close enough to make without much planning, and the apartment itself makes a calm base to return to.

It suits families and groups of up to six who want a central Porto base with room to spread out. Portugal Active's concierge team is available 24/7, arranging excursions or a private chef with 72 hours' notice.

6965339404b96f00147f571a.tagline: A garden studio in Barroselas, minutes from Viana do Castelo
6965339404b96f00147f571a.description:
Buganvílias House is a compact studio apartment with its own private entrance, built around one open-plan room. A double bed sits opposite a kitchenette fitted with stove, microwave, toaster, kettle and coffee maker, and a full bathroom with hairdryer and linens completes the space. Large windows and wooden accents keep the room bright, and a private patio holds an outdoor table and seating with a garden view.

The apartment forms part of Fountain Retreat, a rural estate in Barroselas, just a few minutes from Viana do Castelo in the Minho region. Guests share the estate's pool, tennis court and minigolf, with horseback riding and Viana's museums and town centre within easy reach.

Mornings start at the outdoor table, coffee in hand, with bougainvillea scenting the air. Afternoons might mean a swim in the shared pool or a set of tennis, before an early evening glass of wine back on the patio as the light softens over the garden.

Suited to a couple wanting a quiet, self-contained base near Viana do Castelo, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

6965338ed1c09900156e8502.tagline: A Minho retreat built for long days by the pool and longer evenings around the grill
6965338ed1c09900156e8502.description:
Calejo House sits in Nogueira, near Viana do Castelo, with five bedrooms across a layout designed for groups. Two ground-floor bedrooms (one en-suite) suit those who prefer to skip stairs, while two upstairs rooms catch natural light and garden views. A self-contained mini apartment, with its own entrance, double bedroom, bathroom and kitchen, gives couples or relatives real privacy. Downstairs, a basement holds a billiards room and a wine cellar built to hold around a thousand bottles.

Outside, the garden wraps around two swimming pools, one for adults and one for children, plus a dedicated BBQ area and several seating and dining spots. The setting is Minho at its most rural, within reach of Viana do Castelo's shops, museums and coastline, with cycling, fishing, horseback riding and water sports all available locally.

Days here settle into a rhythm: mornings by the pool, lunch under the garden trees, afternoons on the sports court or with a game of billiards, evenings at the grill with wine from the cellar close at hand.

Calejo House suits families and groups of up to ten who want space to spread out, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

6965338554dbb5001568a505.tagline: A calm balcony apartment on Praça Marquês de Pombal, close to Porto's landmarks
6965338554dbb5001568a505.description:
This one-bedroom apartment pairs clean, minimalist lines with a working balance of comfort: a double bed in the main room, a bright living area with a sofa bed and TV, and a kitchen equipped for anything from coffee and toast to a proper dinner. A private balcony gives the flat its own quiet corner, ideal with a glass of wine as the evening cools.

The address is Praça Marquês de Pombal, a calm square with fast access to the centre. Avenida dos Aliados, Torre dos Clérigos and the Ribeira are all within walking distance, and Marquês metro station is 350 metres away, about five minutes on foot, connecting directly to the airport and train stations.

Mornings suit a slow coffee at the kitchen table before heading out to the cafés and shops nearby. Evenings are for the balcony, watching the square settle as the city's landmarks stay a short stroll away.

Suited to couples wanting a central, unhurried base, with Portugal Active's concierge on call 24/7 for anything from transfers to a private chef, arranged with 72 hours' notice.

696533d2ec19770014fd1b52.tagline: A modern villa steps from Amorosa Beach, with a rooftop view of the Atlantic
696533d2ec19770014fd1b52.description:
Coastal Horizon spreads across several floors, with four bedrooms including a private suite and three bathrooms, one fitted with a hydromassage bathtub. The living room opens through large windows onto the garden, and the kitchen is fully equipped for family cooking. A basement games room holds a pool table and table tennis, while a barbecue area sets up outdoor dining for warm evenings.

The house sits in the village of Amorosa, right in front of the beach, in a quiet, family-friendly stretch of the Minho coast. Cafés, bakeries and restaurants are within walking distance, along with supermarkets, and Viana do Castelo is a ten-minute drive for the city's gastronomy and culture.

Days here settle into rhythm: mornings on the sand a few steps from the door, afternoons at the pool table or over long lunches in the garden, evenings climbing to the rooftop terrace as the light drops over the Atlantic.

Suited to families or groups of up to nine wanting easy beach access with room to spread out, with Portugal Active's concierge on call 24/7 for excursions, private chefs or any request made 72 hours ahead.

696532f3753fb0001424a570.tagline: Countryside calm five minutes from Cabedelo Beach, ten from Viana do Castelo
696532f3753fb0001424a570.description:
Three air-conditioned bedrooms and two bathrooms sleep up to eight across a house built around an open living and dining area, a fully equipped kitchen with dishwasher and washer, and an indoor fireplace for cooler evenings. Outside, a private entrance opens onto a large lawn garden with outdoor seating, sun loungers and a BBQ area.

Cabedelo Beach is a five-minute drive south, ideal for surfers and swimmers, while Viana do Castelo's historic centre sits ten minutes north, with Manuelino architecture, market squares and traditional restaurants. Cycling and horseback riding trails, plus water sports and an aquapark, are all within easy reach.

Mornings suit coffee on the patio before the garden warms up, kids at play on the lawn while adults linger over breakfast. Evenings mean a barbecue outdoors or a fire lit indoors, with the day's catch from Cabedelo or a market find from town on the table.

Suited to families and small groups wanting privacy and space near both coast and city; Portugal Active's concierge is available 24/7, with services best requested 72 hours ahead.

6965335df1c3a8001597c8e4.tagline: A duplex at Cabedelo, 300 metres from the sand
6965335df1c3a8001597c8e4.description:
This duplex in Cabedelo sleeps up to five across two bedrooms, with a queen bed, two singles and a sofa bed to work with. The living area is bright and opens onto a private balcony, and the kitchen is fully equipped for cooking properly rather than just getting by. Free parking and a garage make arriving by car straightforward.

Cabedelo Beach is 300 metres away, and the neighbourhood around it is quiet, safe and set up for an active stay, with bike lanes, local shops and restaurants close by. Viana do Castelo's train station is about 10 minutes by car, and Porto Airport is 60 kilometres south.

Mornings suit coffee on the balcony before the short walk to the beach for a swim or a surf session, the coastline here is well known for both. Evenings are for cooking with produce from nearby shops, or heading out to one of the local restaurants before an easy stroll back.

It suits families or small groups after a straightforward beach base with real infrastructure around it, and Portugal Active's concierge is on call 24/7, with 72 hours' notice appreciated for arranging extras.

6a341163c50f210012f12b80.tagline: A riverside house in Avintes, four bedrooms deep and steps from the Douro.
6a341163c50f210012f12b80.description:
Douro Garden spreads across two floors linked by a solid-wood spiral staircase. Upstairs, the social floor holds a living room with a contemporary fireplace, sofas and a dining table beneath modern artwork, while French doors open onto balconies over the river; the kitchen's corner windows look out to the opposite bank. Downstairs, four air-conditioned bedrooms with wooden flooring include a master suite with a private bathroom, bathtub and granite vanity, two further doubles, and a family room with bunk beds, books and games.

The house sits on the southern bank of the Douro in Avintes, a quiet parish known for its dark Broa de Avintes bread, sold in local bakeries. Porto and the wine cellars of Vila Nova de Gaia are 15 minutes away.

Mornings suit coffee on the balcony, river below, before a walk down the terraced garden. Evenings gather at the tile-decorated barbecue area, charcoal going, dinner laid outside as the water darkens.

Suited to families or groups of up to nine wanting river life close to the city, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

6a3ba1fce19cb0001dc57ea6.tagline: A one-bedroom apartment beside the Cathedral, in the heart of Viana do Castelo
6a3ba1fce19cb0001dc57ea6.description:
Filigree Plaza sits next to the Cathedral in Viana do Castelo's historic centre, a one-bedroom apartment with a queen bed and a living room sofa bed for two, sleeping up to four. The kitchen is fully equipped for proper cooking, with a dining table for shared meals, and the living area holds cable TV and city views from the balcony or patio.

Praça da República and the banks of the Lima River are a short walk from the door, both good for evening walks. The apartment is in a lively, central part of town, with shops and museums nearby; note that August's Romaria de Nossa Senhora d'Agonia brings festivities and higher noise levels to the area.

Mornings suit coffee at the dining table before heading out to the old streets around the Cathedral. Afternoons can be spent exploring downtown or the riverbank, with the kitchen ready for cooking dinner with produce picked up locally, and evenings settling into the living room with the television on.

Suited to couples or small families wanting a central base in Viana do Castelo, with Portugal Active's concierge on hand to arrange horseback riding or a private chef.

69653394ecf7490014ed2ed9.tagline: A rustic Minho studio with pool access, minutes from Viana do Castelo's historic centre.
69653394ecf7490014ed2ed9.description:
Fountain Cottage is a compact studio within the Fountain Retreat I Pool & Sports Escape, built for two. The open-plan interior pairs a double bed with a small kitchenette and a full bathroom, finished in rustic style with plenty of natural light. Outside, a private patio opens onto shared gardens and the estate's communal pool.

The retreat sits in Barroselas, in the Minho countryside just a few minutes from Viana do Castelo. Village life here moves at its own pace, with local shops, family-run restaurants and seasonal fairs nearby, while green hills and valleys offer trails and bike paths for those who want to explore on foot or wheel. Viana do Castelo's historic centre, including the Santa Luzia Basilica, is a short drive away.

Days start slowly, coffee on the patio with the sound of the countryside for company, and end by the pool as the light softens over the fields. In between, there is little reason to rush.

Suited to couples wanting a quiet rural base near Viana do Castelo, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

6965339dbf04fe0013743e2d.tagline: Five houses, one estate, in the Minho countryside near Viana do Castelo
6965339dbf04fe0013743e2d.description:
Fountain Retreat gathers five independent houses across one rural estate, together holding 12 bedrooms, 13 bathrooms and space for up to 28 guests. The two studio houses, Granjas and Buganvílias, suit couples with their open-plan layouts and kitchenettes. Jardim House and Rosas House add separate bedrooms and living rooms with sofa beds for families. Senhorial House anchors the property with seven suites, a fireplace lounge and a billiard room in the basement.

The estate sits in Barroselas, a short drive from Viana do Castelo in the Minho region, set among gardens with century-old trees and walking trails. A tennis court and mini golf course sit alongside the outdoor pool, giving the grounds a genuine sense of space.

Days here settle into their own rhythm: mornings around the pool or wandering the garden paths, afternoons on the tennis court or mini golf, evenings gathered in the Senhorial lounge with the fire lit and the billiard table in play downstairs.

It suits large families or groups travelling together across generations, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533a0ecf7490014ed31d5.tagline: A garden cottage near Barroselas, with pool access and Viana do Castelo close by
696533a0ecf7490014ed31d5.description:
Garden House is a compact stone-built cottage on the Fountain Retreat estate, with one double bedroom, a sofa bed in the living area for extra guests, and a kitchenette fitted with fridge, stovetop, microwave and coffee machine. A dining table looks out over the garden, and the bathroom sits just outside the bedroom, off the shared hallway. Outside, a private furnished terrace opens onto flowering grounds, with access to the estate's outdoor pool.

The house sits in Barroselas, a few minutes from Viana do Castelo, in the heart of the Minho countryside. Village life here runs on local shops, weekly fairs and family-run restaurants, while trails and bike paths trace the surrounding hills. Viana do Castelo's historic centre and the Santa Luzia Basilica are a short drive away.

Mornings might start with coffee on the terrace, garden air still cool, before a walk into Barroselas for bread and conversation. Evenings call for a swim, then dinner at the outdoor table as the fields darken around you.

Suited to couples or small families wanting a quiet rural base, with Portugal Active's local team on hand for anything needed.

696533b7bf04fe00137440f8.tagline: A duplex loft in Guimarães' old town, where Portugal itself began
696533b7bf04fe00137440f8.description:
Heritage Loft I occupies a stylish duplex in the heart of Guimarães, with a queen bed tucked on the mezzanine and a bright lower floor holding a sofa, TV, dining table and fully equipped kitchenette. The bathroom is spacious and contemporary, with a walk-in shower, and wooden details and natural light give the whole apartment a warm, lived-in feel. It sleeps up to three.

You're inside Guimarães' UNESCO-listed historic centre, cobbled streets away from the Castle, the Ducal Palace and Largo da Oliveira. Parque de Camões parking is an 8-minute walk, the railway station about 15, and local buses stop nearby for onward trips around the Minho.

Mornings start with coffee at the dining table as light comes through the windows, before a short walk out into the old town's cafés and squares. Evenings are for wandering back through quiet cobbled lanes past centuries-old monuments to the loft's calm.

Suited to couples or small families wanting to be steps from the birthplace of Portugal, with Portugal Active's local team and 24/7 concierge on hand for anything booked 72 hours ahead.

69653388753fb0001424abad.tagline: A private terrace, a jacuzzi, and Cedofeita at your door
69653388753fb0001424abad.description:
Invictus Escape is a two-level apartment built around an open-plan living area, where the lounge sits alongside a fully equipped kitchen. The main bedroom holds a double bed with quiet, understated decor, while a mezzanine reached by an interior staircase adds a second sleeping space for up to four guests. Its private terrace, fitted with its own jacuzzi, is the apartment's real asset — an outdoor room of your own in the middle of the city.

The apartment sits on Rua dos Bragas, a quiet street in Cedofeita, close to independent cafés, restaurants and galleries. Rua de Cedofeita and the Crystal Palace Gardens are a short walk away, and Aliados metro station, with links to the airport and Campanhã station, is about nine minutes on foot.

Mornings start with coffee from the kitchen before heading out to Cedofeita's streets and shops. Evenings are for coming back to the terrace, sinking into the jacuzzi, and letting the city's noise settle into the background.

Suited to couples or small groups after a stylish base with a private outdoor feature, it comes with Portugal Active's 24/7 concierge, from local excursions to private chefs, with 72 hours' notice.

69653390ecf7490014ed2d6c.tagline: Beachfront calm in Carreço, a kilometre from Montedor Lighthouse
69653390ecf7490014ed2d6c.description:
Lighthouse View sits right at the water's edge in Carreço, its panoramic living room window framing the Atlantic. Three bedrooms and two bathrooms sleep up to six, with a fully equipped kitchen, dining table and a sun-drenched terrace built for long lunches outdoors. A garden gives a quieter spot for an evening glass of wine, with direct access to the coastal trails beyond.

Montedor Lighthouse is less than a kilometre away, and Carreço Beach a short stroll. The historic centre of Viana do Castelo is 10 minutes by car, while the Northern Coastal Ecotrail and the Sanctuary of Santa Luzia are both within easy reach, along with local cafés and restaurants serving typical Minho fare.

Mornings start with coffee on the terrace, sea air drifting in before a walk down to the beach or along the dunes. Afternoons suit cycling the coastal paths or driving into Viana do Castelo for museums and shopping. Evenings settle back into the garden, sky over the water fading as dinner cooks in a well-stocked kitchen.

Suited to families or friends wanting an uncomplicated coastal base, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533714b583900135cef22.tagline: A step-free country house in Cardielos, five kilometres from Viana do Castelo.
696533714b583900135cef22.description:
Six suites, each with its own bathroom, make up this single-level house in Cardielos: five with queen beds, one with two singles, all designed with step-free access, wide doorways and grab-rails for guests who need them. The lounge has a fireplace for cooler evenings, the kitchen is fully equipped, and air conditioning covers the warmer months.

Cardielos sits five kilometres from the centre of Viana do Castelo, in the heart of the Minho, surrounded by open countryside and rolling hills. It is a quiet base for exploring the Lima river valley and the coast beyond, well away from traffic and crowds.

Days here settle into their own rhythm: coffee outside near the garden's saltwater cascade, children occupied at the private playground, an afternoon by the shared pool when the sun is out, and a barbecue supper at the outdoor dining table before the fire is lit indoors.

Suited to families or groups of up to twelve travelling together, with the Portugal Active team on hand locally for anything the stay requires.

696533616cff760015e28802.tagline: Two suites in Cardielos, a saltwater waterfall garden, 5 km from Viana do Castelo
696533616cff760015e28802.description:
Two suites, each with a queen-size bed and private bathroom, sit within a house built for calm rather than crowds. The kitchen is fully equipped for group cooking, and outside a saltwater waterfall gives the garden its own quiet soundtrack, alongside shared access to an infinity pool, outdoor dining area with barbecue, and a children's playground.

The house is in Cardielos, 5 km from the centre of Viana do Castelo, in a rural pocket of the Minho known for rolling hills and green fields. The surrounding countryside suits cycling and horseback riding, while Viana do Castelo itself holds the Basilica of Santa Luzia and a good spread of restaurants and shopping.

Days here move at their own pace: coffee at the outdoor dining table, a swim in the shared pool before the heat sets in, an afternoon cycling the lanes around Cardielos or exploring Viana do Castelo's old town, and evenings back at the barbecue with the waterfall running in the background as the garden cools.

It suits families or small groups of up to four wanting a peaceful base near the coast, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

69e7552df2f71100122bbb35.tagline: A riverside duplex in Cabedelo, ferry-ride from Viana's old town
69e7552df2f71100122bbb35.description:
Lumina Duplex spans two floors linked by a spiral staircase. The main level holds an open-plan living and dining area, with a kitchen fitted with integrated Balay and Teka appliances — induction hob, oven, dishwasher — plus a guest WC. Downstairs, two double bedrooms have light oak flooring and a full bathroom with a walk-in shower. A private garage space and lift access complete the setup.

The apartment sits in Cabedelo, Viana do Castelo's riverside quarter where the Lima estuary meets the Atlantic. Cabedelo beach is under ten minutes on foot, and the passenger ferry crosses to the historic centre — Praça da República, the pelourinho, the cathedral — in five minutes.

Large windows face the estuary, and at dusk the light catches the Santa Luzia Basilica on the hill opposite. Mornings suit a walk to the fish market or the beach; evenings, the short ferry crossing for dinner by the waterfront.

Suited to couples or small families wanting a base between river and ocean, with Portugal Active's concierge available around the clock.

696533d34b583900135cfd96.tagline: Two villas, one Alto Minho estate — pool, sauna and jacuzzi for up to 23
696533d34b583900135cfd96.description:
The retreat pairs two adjoining villas: The Luxury Manor, seven bedrooms each with a private bathroom, a fireplace living room with a piano, a dining room and a full kitchen; and The Nature Princess, two bright bedrooms with its own jacuzzi, sauna and pool. Together they hold nine bedrooms, ten bathrooms and space for up to 23 guests, linked by shared gardens.

Set in Alto Minho, the estate is ringed by mountains and valleys near the Vez River. Arcos de Valdevez's historic centre, with its restaurants and shops, is minutes away, and the Passadiços das Lagoas do Vez, Peneda-Gerês National Park and riverside beaches are all close by.

Mornings suit a swim in the private pool or coffee in the garden before the day's plans. Evenings gather at the piano by the fireplace, or in the sauna and jacuzzi, with a barbecue to close things out.

It suits large families, groups and celebrations wanting two houses' worth of space under one roof, with Portugal Active's 24-hour concierge arranging chefs or excursions given 72 hours' notice.

6970af61638a8a0015eaa850.tagline: Beachfront in Moledo, three suites deep, with a pool that faces the sunset
6970af61638a8a0015eaa850.description:
Moledo Front Beach sits directly on the sand, with three suites and five bathrooms sleeping up to six. The open-plan living space is built for light — high ceilings, large windows, and a terrace that looks straight out to sea. Outside, a private pool and garden give guests their own stretch of coastline without leaving the property.

Moledo Beach is a short stroll away, ranked among Europe's top 20 by Condé Nast Traveller. Local restaurants serving fresh seafood and traditional Portuguese cooking are five to ten minutes on foot, with shops just steps from the door. The historic town of Caminha is a short drive further, for a change of pace.

Mornings start with coffee on the terrace, the Atlantic laid out below. Afternoons run to the beach and back to the pool, evenings to the terrace again as the sky over Moledo turns for sunset.

Suited to families or small groups wanting a proper beach base, with Portugal Active's concierge on call 24/7 for chefs, tours, or anything else, given 72 hours' notice.

6965334abf04fe0013742da8.tagline: A stone-and-timber lodge on Serra D'Arga, with the Lima valley spread out below.
6965334abf04fe0013742da8.description:
Montaria Lodge sits on the slopes of Serra D'Arga, a stone and timber house built for groups who want space without losing comfort. Six bedrooms sleep up to twelve guests beneath a vaulted wooden ceiling, with wide glass doors opening onto views over the Lima valley. The kitchen is fully equipped, the living areas generous, and outside a private pool sits in the garden with sun loungers and an outdoor dining area.

The village of Montaria moves slowly, its stone-cobbled lanes threading past old quintas and apple orchards. Mountain trails lead to waterfalls and lagoons for those willing to walk or cycle further. Ponte de Lima, with its fortnightly market, is ten minutes by car; Viana do Castelo, with its historic centre and the Basilica of Santa Luzia, is under twenty. The Atlantic coast is just over half an hour away.

Mornings start with coffee at the glass doors, the valley still catching the light. Afternoons are for the pool or the trails; evenings for watching the sun drop behind the peaks from the garden.

Suited to families and groups after real quiet, with the Portugal Active concierge on call for anything arranged in advance.

696533794fe6a100145fe4bf.tagline: A beach-step apartment in Cabedelo, with a balcony built for long barbecue evenings
696533794fe6a100145fe4bf.description:
This one-bedroom apartment sits within a private condominium in Cabedelo, moments from the beach. The bedroom holds a double bed, while the living room's sofa bed brings capacity to three, useful for a family stay. A balcony with a barbecue and garden view opens off the living space, and the kitchen comes properly equipped, from dishwasher to toaster, for cooking in rather than dining out.

Cabedelo lies a few minutes from Viana do Castelo's centre, with the golden sands and Atlantic surf right on the doorstep. The area is known for surfing, kitesurfing and paddleboarding, and for the bike paths and walking trails that run along the coast. Viana do Castelo train station is about a ten-minute drive away.

Days here settle into an easy rhythm: coffee on the balcony before the beach, an afternoon on a paddleboard or bike path, then back for a barbecue as the light fades and the sea breeze picks up. Seaside cafés nearby cover the nights you'd rather not cook.

It suits couples or small families wanting a straightforward coastal base, with Portugal Active's concierge on call 24/7 for anything from excursions to a private chef, given 72 hours' notice.

696532fa6d209c001510d5ee.tagline: A duplex by the river mouth, five minutes from Cabedelo Beach on foot.
696532fa6d209c001510d5ee.description:
This duplex apartment spreads across two floors in Viana do Castelo, with 2 bedrooms and 1 bathroom for up to 4 guests. The living area opens onto a private balcony over the river, and the kitchen and dining space are properly equipped for real cooking rather than just reheating. A private garden and free on-site parking round out the practical side.

Cabedelo Beach is a 5-minute walk away, Rodanho Beach 14 minutes on foot. Viana do Castelo's historic centre and the Shipyards sit 6 km away by car — close enough for an afternoon, far enough to keep the mornings quiet.

Days here settle into a rhythm: coffee on the balcony as the river catches the light, then down to Cabedelo for a swim or a surf before the town wakes up properly. Evenings mean the same walk back, slower, timed for the sunset.

Suited to couples or a small family who want the beach at the door and a base to explore Minho from; Portugal Active's local team is on call 24/7 for anything from a private chef to airport transfers.

6965333104b96f00147f5428.tagline: A townhouse in Viana do Castelo, steps from the river and the old town.
6965333104b96f00147f5428.description:
This townhouse sits in the heart of Viana do Castelo, with three bedrooms and two bathrooms for up to eight guests. A garden with BBQ grill and outdoor seating opens off the house, and an indoor fireplace gives the living space its winter centre. City and garden views frame the rooms, and a private entrance keeps the house self-contained.

The Minho region unfolds from the doorstep. Supermarkets and local restaurants are a short walk away, along with a river beach and an ecological park, while the historic downtown and its museums and shops sit close by.

Mornings start with coffee and a walk down to the river beach before the town wakes properly. Evenings belong to the garden — something on the grill, plates passed round the outdoor table, then the fireplace lit as the air cools.

It suits families or friends wanting a real base in Viana do Castelo rather than a hotel room, with Portugal Active's local team on call for transfers, a private chef or any other arrangement, given 72 hours' notice.

696532eee44e1a0015bb2460.tagline: A quiet beach flat by Cabedelo, steps from the surf and sand.
696532eee44e1a0015bb2460.description:
The apartment covers 80 square metres on a single level, with one bedroom and an open-plan kitchen kept bright and unfussy. A private garden with outdoor furniture sits alongside a terrace, and air conditioning and heating cover both ends of the year. The kitchen is fully equipped for home cooking.

It sits in a quiet corner of Viana do Castelo, right next to Cabedelo Beach — the surf, sand and sea a short walk from the door. Porto Airport is 60 km south, close enough for an easy transfer without the crowds of a city stay.

Mornings start with coffee on the terrace before the short walk down to Cabedelo for a swim or a surf. Afternoons suit cycling along the coast or reading in the garden, and evenings settle back onto the terrace as the light fades over the beach.

It suits couples or small families after a simple beach base rather than a resort, with Portugal Active's local team available for anything from private chef bookings to airport transfers.

696533266dec35001492fdbb.tagline: Steps from Cabedelo Beach, built for mornings in the surf and evenings on the balcony
696533266dec35001492fdbb.description:
A recently renovated one-bedroom apartment on Avenida do Cabedelo, with a king-sized bed, a sofa bed in the living room, and a private entrance and balcony. The kitchen is fully equipped for real cooking, and the building has a lift and free parking, making arrival simple.

Cabedelo Beach is a few steps away, one of the Minho coast's known stretches for surfing and kitesurfing. Restaurants, shops and services in Viana do Castelo are a short drive off, and bus stops nearby connect to the historic centre. Porto's Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport is around 60 minutes by car.

Mornings suit a walk or cycle along the shore before the wind picks up; afternoons belong to the water, whether that is surfing off the beach or simply watching it from the balcony. Evenings settle into the living room, or a table booked nearby for Minho cooking.

Suited to couples or a small family after a beach base with real independence, backed by Portugal Active's concierge, available for local arrangements with 72 hours' notice.

6965332327950e001416f0b2.tagline: A seven-bedroom lodge near Cabedelo beach, built for big groups and open water
6965332327950e001416f0b2.description:
This semi-detached villa in Viana do Castelo holds seven bedrooms and four bathrooms across eleven beds, three of them king-size, with two living rooms and an office for those who need to work a morning away. A garden wraps the property, parking runs to three cars, and the heated outdoor pool (heating available on request, minimum five days) anchors the terrace alongside a table tennis table.

Praia do Cabedelo is close by, a beach known internationally for windsurfing and kitesurfing, and the city centre of Viana do Castelo sits within easy reach for cafes, restaurants and shops. Surf schools, kitesurfing lessons and a water park are all nearby.

Days here tend to split between pool and sea: mornings on the water at Cabedelo, afternoons back at the villa with lunch cooked in the fully equipped kitchen, evenings in the themed living room with its game consoles and portable sound system while the group unwinds.

It suits families or groups of up to fourteen wanting space and water sports on their doorstep, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533494b9b64001401b62e.tagline: A rustic farmhouse retreat between the Lima River and the Minho hills
696533494b9b64001401b62e.description:
Oliveira's Farm spreads five bedrooms across a rustic-style farmhouse — two with queen beds, one king, and two twin rooms sharing four singles — plus five full bathrooms and a separate guest WC. The living room holds a chess table and board games, while a dedicated games room adds a pool table, foosball and cards. Outside, a private pool sits within a garden thick with fruit trees.

The farm lies in the countryside outside Viana do Castelo, 12 km from the town centre. Cabedelo Beach, known for windsurfing, kitesurfing and surfing, is 8.7 km away, the Lima River just 2.1 km, and Valinhas Park 15 km. Pharmacies and supermarkets are close by.

Mornings might mean coffee on the patio before a walk down to the stream that runs through the grounds, or picking fruit straight from the trees. Afternoons settle into the pool or a game of pool table in the games room, and evenings end with a barbecue in the outdoor dining area as the garden cools.

Suited to families or groups of up to ten wanting space and quiet, with Portugal Active's concierge on hand for anything from excursions to a private chef.

69c415701b964f00157188bd.tagline: A 300-year-old granite watermill on the Coura, with its own river beach at the door.
69c415701b964f00157188bd.description:
River Beach Loft occupies a granite watermill built three centuries ago in Vilar de Mouros, once a stopover for Bob Dylan. The loft holds a queen bed, a desk for quiet work, a sofa bed, a small kitchenette, a dining table and a full bathroom, all finished in stone and timber. Step outside and you are on the bank of the Coura River, with direct access to its public beach.

The Coura curves around the property, forming a clear, calm river beach with sandy banks. Vilar de Mouros itself is a quiet riverside village known for hosting Portugal's oldest music festival. Caminha, with its medieval centre, Clock Tower and ferry to Spain, is 5 km away; La Guardia, across the border, is 20 km.

Mornings begin with the sound of water over rocks and coffee at the garden table. Afternoons call for a swim off the river beach or a walk along the Coura. Evenings settle into the garden, dinner outdoors, granite walls holding the day's warmth.

Suited to couples or a small family after quiet, water and history, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

69c415701b964f00157188b5.tagline: A 300-year-old watermill on the Coura River, once home to Joe Cocker
69c415701b964f00157188b5.description:
Granite and old timber shape this 300-year-old watermill, set directly on the Coura River with its own stretch of river beach. Two bedrooms sleep four: a double for quiet nights, twins for restful ones, sharing one well-appointed bathroom. There is no kitchen here — the house is built for rest, not cooking, with a garden that runs down to the water.

The river curves generously around the property, forming clear, sandy-banked waters good for summer swimming. Vilar de Mouros, the riverside village nearby, hosts Portugal's oldest music festival and otherwise offers little but water and silence. Caminha, with its medieval centre, Clock Tower and ferry to Spain, is 5km away; La Guardia, across the border in Spain, is 20km.

Mornings mean coffee to the sound of the Coura moving over rock, then a walk to the beach for a swim before the day warms. Evenings settle into the garden, watching light fade over the water with nothing else on the agenda.

Suited to couples or a small family wanting genuine quiet, with Portugal Active's local team on hand for anything needed.

69ca869e5b0a0500158b7d5a.tagline: A riverfront apartment on the Lima, ten minutes from Viana's old town
69ca869e5b0a0500158b7d5a.description:
Fully renovated in 2026, this two-bedroom apartment sits on Viana do Castelo's riverfront avenue, with the Lima River and green hills beyond visible from its windows. Two queen-size bedrooms sleep up to four: one warm in tone with a dark headboard and terracotta cushions, the other lighter, with botanical wallpaper and mustard accents. Crisp white linens, folded bathrobes and a fully equipped kitchen give it the finish of a boutique hotel.

The historic centre is ten minutes on foot, past the municipal market and the azulejo-lined Praça da República. Riverside, the promenade carries cyclists, families and the odd passing boat. Meadela and Areosa, with their quintas and local festivals, are minutes away, and the Atlantic coast is under ten minutes by car.

Mornings open with the Lima below the window, the horizon of water and hills the first thing you see. Evenings suit the tascas of the old quarter, where caldo verde comes before the bacalhau, or a slower one at home with the river for company.

Suited to couples or small families wanting a city base with a river view, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

69c415701b964f00157188ad.tagline: A 300-year-old watermill on the Coura River, with its own path to the water
69c415701b964f00157188ad.description:
This is a restored 18th-century watermill in Vilar de Mouros, its granite walls and walnut-tone floors framing four bedrooms — three with queen beds, one twin — each with a full bathroom. A glass panel in the floor reveals the original mill mechanism below. The open-plan living area looks over the river, the kitchen is fully equipped with a dishwasher, and dinners gather under a handcrafted chandelier.

The Coura River curves around the property, forming a clear river beach reached by a private path. Vilar de Mouros, a quiet village known for hosting Portugal's oldest music festival, sits 5 km from Caminha's medieval centre and Clock Tower, with the Atlantic coast 10 km away and Spain's La Guardia 20 km further.

Mornings start with the sound of water over rocks and coffee on the terrace. Afternoons mean swimming from the river beach in summer, or a barbecue on the house's own indoor grill. Evenings settle by the fireplace or out on the garden terrace as the light fades over the water.

Suited to families or two couples wanting a quiet, rural base, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533b2e44e1a0015bb2b42.tagline: A moored boat on the Lima River, steps from Viana do Castelo's old town.
696533b2e44e1a0015bb2b42.description:
The Rose Dream Boat is a one-bedroom vessel moored on the Lima River, with a cozy double cabin and a second sleeping area with two single beds, suiting up to four guests. The living space holds a kitchenette with a coffee machine, small oven and gas stove, plus a compact fridge, and a private bathroom completes the layout. Outdoor seating on deck lets you take the river air without leaving the boat.

The boat sits in the centre of Viana do Castelo, close to the historic quarter with its traditional shops, cafés and restaurants known for the region's cooking. Museums and the old streets are a short walk away, and the Lima River runs right past your door.

Mornings start with coffee on deck, watching the water and the town wake up. By evening, it's a few minutes' walk into the historic centre for dinner, then back to the boat to sit outside as the lights come on along the river. The vessel stays moored throughout your stay, for safety.

It suits couples or a small family after something different from a standard apartment, with Portugal Active's concierge on call 24/7 for anything from a private chef to local excursions, requested 72 hours ahead.

69653398bf04fe0013743b98.tagline: A Barroselas cottage with garden, shared pool and Minho's hills close by.
69653398bf04fe0013743b98.description:
Roses House pairs two double bedrooms with a shower room off one of them, a living area with a sofa bed and dining table, and a kitchenette fitted with fridge, stove, microwave, toaster and coffee machine. A small furnished terrace opens onto the garden, and air conditioning, heating and Wi-Fi cover the practical side of things.

The house sits in Barroselas, a Minho village a short drive from Viana do Castelo and its Santa Luzia Basilica. Around it, green hills and valleys carry walking and cycling trails, and the village itself keeps a rhythm of local fairs and family-run restaurants.

Mornings suit coffee on the terrace with the garden for company; afternoons might mean a trail on foot or by bike, or a stretch by the shared outdoor pool before the evening cools. Horseback riding is available nearby for those who want it.

It suits families or small groups happy to share pool and garden with the neighbouring house, with Portugal Active's local team on hand for arrival and anything the stay needs.

6a3a63f9e19cb0001db6a05e.tagline: A studio on the Cabedelo peninsula, between river, pines and Atlantic swell
6a3a63f9e19cb0001db6a05e.description:
Saltwind Studio sits on the Cabedelo peninsula, a compact apartment built around a bright living room with dining table, sofa bed and balcony. The bedroom holds a double bed and built-in closets with its own balcony access, and the bathroom keeps a proper bathtub alongside an LED-backlit mirror. The kitchen is fully equipped, from oven to dishwasher, so cooking with market fish is straightforward.

Cabedelo Beach is a short walk away, its Atlantic swell known to surfers, kitesurfers and windsurfers, backed by century-old pine groves and the mouth of the Lima River. From the balcony, Monte de Santa Luzia rises across the water, crowned by the Sacred Heart of Jesus Sanctuary, one of Minho's landmarks. Restaurants serving Minho coast seafood and small local shops sit within easy reach.

Mornings suit coffee on the balcony before the wind picks up along the beach; evenings call for a glass of wine as the light catches the Monte. Warm afternoons drift between café terraces and sand.

Suited to a couple or small family wanting Cabedelo's beach and river on their doorstep, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533814b9b64001401c7b8.tagline: A beachfront house in Carreço, close to Viana do Castelo, built for slow coastal days
696533814b9b64001401c7b8.description:
Salty Escape sits right on the water in Carreço, with sea views from its terrace and direct beach access. Three double bedrooms and two bathrooms sleep up to six, and the open dining table and fully equipped kitchen make it easy to cook and eat together. Outside, a private terrace holds both a dining set and a barbecue, with air conditioning and free parking to keep things simple year-round.

Carreço is a small coastal village a few minutes from Viana do Castelo, with its own train station within walking distance for onward trips along the Minho coast. The Atlantic is on the doorstep, with fishing, cycling and water sports all close by, and the town itself offers museums and shopping for slower afternoons.

Mornings here start with coffee on the terrace, the sea within sight and earshot. Afternoons might mean a walk to the beach or a cycle along the coast, and evenings settle into barbecue dinners outdoors as the light fades over the water.

Salty Escape suits families or small groups who want the coast without compromise, with Portugal Active's concierge team on call 24/7 for anything from excursions to a private chef, arranged with 72 hours' notice.

696533762def930014e917bf.tagline: Steps from Cabedelo Beach, a duplex built for surf boards, salt air and easy mornings.
696533762def930014e917bf.description:
Seabreeze Duplex is a three-bedroom apartment arranged over two floors, with a double room and a twin room upstairs and a bunk room on the ground floor, plus two bathrooms split between levels. The décor is minimalist and uncluttered, the kitchen fully equipped, and the living area set up with clear seating and dining zones. A private terrace with a barbecue extends the house outdoors, with space to store surf and kite boards alongside the loungers.

The apartment sits close to Praia do Cabedelo, known internationally for windsurfing, kitesurfing and surfing, in a quiet residential pocket away from the busiest stretches. Viana do Castelo's centre, with its cafés and restaurants, is a short distance away, and water parks and surf schools operate nearby.

Mornings start on the terrace with coffee before the boards come out and the short walk to Cabedelo's breaks. Afternoons drift between the beach and the town centre; evenings return to the terrace for a barbecue as the light fades over the garden.

Suited to families or small groups who want the beach on their doorstep, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533752def930014e9167c.tagline: Three bedrooms, one balcony, five hundred metres of sand between you and the Atlantic.
696533752def930014e9167c.description:
This apartment sleeps six across three double bedrooms, with a bright living room opening onto a private balcony and a fully equipped kitchen for cooking at your own pace. A Smart TV, air conditioning and reliable Wi-Fi cover the essentials; the fireplace is decorative only, not in use.

Esposende Beach is 500 metres away, known locally for its water sports, and the Northern Littoral Natural Park lies within easy reach for walks through dunes and coastal habitat. The town itself, in the Minho region, keeps its markets and culinary traditions very much alive.

Mornings suit a walk down to the sand before the town wakes, coffee from the apartment's own kit if you'd rather not rush. Evenings work well on the balcony, watching the light change over the rooftops before heading out to one of Esposende's local restaurants.

Suited to families or small groups wanting a seaside base with urban convenience, with Portugal Active's concierge on call 24/7 for anything from tours to a private chef, given 72 hours' notice.

6965339bbf04fe0013743cd8.tagline: A seven-bedroom manor in Minho, where garden terraces meet games-room evenings.
6965339bbf04fe0013743cd8.description:
Set across two floors and a basement, this manor house holds seven bedrooms, each with its own bathroom, sleeping up to fourteen. The main floor opens onto a bright living room and a fully equipped kitchen with a proper dining table for long meals. Below, a games room with a pool table and foosball table keeps evenings going, alongside a garden, outdoor pool and covered parking.

The house sits in Barroselas, a village of quiet streets and local shops a few minutes from Viana do Castelo. Around it, the Minho countryside unfolds in green hills and valleys, with horseback riding available nearby and small museums to visit further afield.

Mornings start on the terrace, coffee in hand, looking out over garden and fields. Afternoons drift between the pool and the shade of the garden; evenings gather the group indoors for a home-cooked meal, then downstairs for a round of pool or foosball before the fire is lit.

It suits families or groups of up to fourteen wanting space, privacy and a shared table, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533cf4b583900135cfb02.tagline: A duplex by the sea in Esposende, where the ocean and river meet
696533cf4b583900135cfb02.description:
Shoreline Escape is a duplex apartment on Avenida dos Banhos, arranged over two floors for both gathering and privacy. The main level holds a living room with sofa, armchairs and Smart TV, opening onto a balcony with sea views. Three bedrooms — two with doubles, one with a bunk bed — and two full bathrooms with showers sleep up to seven, with a fully equipped kitchen and dining area for family meals.

The beach is a few metres away, and the neighbourhood keeps its own quiet rhythm around cafés, seafood restaurants and bakeries. Esposende's waterfront promenade runs between the Atlantic and the Cávado River, good for a walk or cycle in either direction. The bus terminal, 1.5km off, connects on to Viana do Castelo, Braga and Porto.

Mornings suit the balcony, coffee in hand, sea below. Evenings call for the local seafood spots nearby, then back to unwind with the ocean still in view.

Suited to families or groups wanting a beachside base, with Portugal Active's concierge on call 24/7 for tours or a private chef, given 72 hours' notice.

6a7afc0488f86b001316efa9.tagline: Riverside calm in Barreiro, a ferry crossing from Lisbon.
6a7afc0488f86b001316efa9.description:
Sky Pool Luxury sits within the Nooba development in Barreiro, a two-bedroom apartment with queen beds in each room, two full bathrooms and a guest WC. The open-plan living and dining area opens to a balcony, and the building shares a pool with views over the Tagus.

Barreiro's ferry terminal is a short walk away, putting Lisbon within easy reach across the river. Around the apartment, small restaurants and cafés line streets close to the water, alongside convenience stores and everyday services.

Mornings start with coffee on the balcony before the ferry crossing into the city. Afternoons return to the pool deck, where the Tagus stretches out below. Evenings suit a walk to one of the nearby riverside restaurants for dinner.

The apartment suits couples or small families based in Barreiro or exploring Lisbon by ferry, with Portugal Active's local team managing arrival and any requests.

696533aaf142270014026d70.tagline: Five-storey calm above Viana do Castelo, pool and Atlantic light included
696533aaf142270014026d70.description:
Skyline Retreat spreads across four levels, with five en-suite bedrooms, air conditioning throughout, and private balconies that catch views over the city and out toward the Atlantic. Downstairs, a bright living and dining area opens onto a garden terrace with a pool, outdoor dining table and barbecue, while the fitted kitchen, elevator, gym and garage add the practical comforts of a proper base rather than a mere holiday let.

You're in Viana do Castelo, in Portugal's Minho region, with cycling routes, fishing and water sports close by, plus museums and shops in town for slower afternoons — horseback riding is also on offer for those who want to see the countryside at a different pace.

Days start on the balcony with coffee and the skyline below, move through long lunches at the outdoor table, and settle into evenings by the pool as the light drops over the rooftops. The kitchen, properly equipped, makes it easy to cook together rather than eat out every night.

Suited to families or groups of up to eight who want space and view without giving up convenience, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

6965332c6d209c001510e1c1.tagline: A quiet stone house among the vineyards of the Minho, ten minutes from Ponte de Lima
6965332c6d209c001510e1c1.description:
This four-bedroom house sits among vineyards, forest and mountains in Moreira do Lima, its rooms opening onto a garden and private pool. Inside, a mix of double and single beds sleeps up to ten, with a dining table, wood-burning fireplace and a kitchen built for cooking slowly rather than quickly.

A small clear river runs nearby, reached on foot along local trails, and a traditional tapas restaurant sits within easy reach. Ponte de Lima, Portugal's oldest village, is under ten minutes by car, while the beaches of Viana do Castelo and the entrance to Peneda-Gerês National Park are both a manageable drive away.

Mornings start slowly here, coffee on the patio with the mountains still in shadow. Afternoons might mean a swim, a bike ride along quiet lanes, or a game of ping pong in the garden before the light softens for an evening by the fire.

Suited to families or groups wanting space and stillness in equal measure, with Portugal Active's local team on hand for anything the stay requires.

69653381bf04fe00137437cd.tagline: Stone architecture, a private pool, and the Minho coast within easy reach
69653381bf04fe00137437cd.description:
Stone by the Sea is a two-storey house built in traditional Minho stone, its lines kept clean and uncluttered inside. Four bedrooms and three and a half bathrooms sleep up to eight, with a fully equipped kitchen, dining table, and an indoor fireplace for cooler evenings. Outside, a private pool sits among gardens shaded by olive trees, with a barbecue area and outdoor seating for meals in the open air. A games room with foosball and pool table, plus bicycles for guests, round out the practical extras.

The house is set in Afife, a village a few minutes from Viana do Castelo in the Minho region, where green hills run down to the Atlantic. The area is known for its walking trails, wide sandy beaches, and a slower, coastal pace, with horse riding and water sports both accessible nearby.

Mornings might start with coffee on the patio, hills on one side and the sea somewhere beyond them, before a walk down to the coast. Afternoons settle around the pool or a match on the pool table, and evenings end with something grilled outside and a fire lit once the air cools.

It suits families or groups of up to eight who want space, garden, and coast together, with Portugal Active's team on hand for anything from a private chef to local excursions.

6a4297f706510a0014f79dd1.tagline: Granite, pine and Atlantic light above Carreço’s coast
6a4297f706510a0014f79dd1.description:
Built in granite and wood, this four-bedroom villa in Carreço sits close to the Atlantic, its rooms bright and open to the outdoors. The primary suite has an adjoining room suited to families, and there are 2.5 bathrooms for up to nine guests. A wooden deck frames the private pool, with a lawn garden and terrace looking out to the sea, and an indoor fireplace for cooler evenings.

Carreço is a quiet, residential pocket of Viana do Castelo, in Portugal's Minho region, where coastal trails begin just minutes from the door. The northern light here has its own quality, and the surrounding green hills make for easy walking at sunrise or late afternoon.

Mornings might start on the terrace with coffee and that ocean view, before a walk along the nearby trails while the light is still soft. Afternoons settle into the pool and garden, board games or a book for the children, and evenings gather round the fireplace as the Atlantic breeze picks up.

Suited to families or groups wanting a private, coastal base, with Portugal Active's concierge on hand throughout the stay.

6a312c59a705e1001327708c.tagline: Duplex living above Nazaré's cliffs, with the Atlantic at every window
6a312c59a705e1001327708c.description:
Sunset Cliffs with Ocean View is a two-floor duplex with five en-suite bedrooms, built for groups who want space without sacrificing privacy. The upper floor holds the master suite with direct terrace access, a living room and dining area facing the ocean, and a fully equipped kitchen with coffee machine. Below, four further suites offer rain showers and marble-effect finishes, linked by a glass-balustrade staircase that keeps the whole house filled with light.

The house sits atop the cliffs in a private, quiet condominium, with coastal vegetation and the sound of waves for company. Nazaré's centre and Praia do Norte, famed for its giant waves, are minutes away, along with the funicular linking the beach to the clifftop Sítio district and the town's seafood restaurants.

Mornings suit coffee on the terrace with the Atlantic laid out below; evenings might mean a game of snooker or foosball in the condominium's games room before dinner on the waterfront in town.

Suited to families or groups of up to ten, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533d8753fb0001424b10d.tagline: A modern retreat by the Vez River, with sauna, hot tub and pool for two.
696533d8753fb0001424b10d.description:
Set within Quinta de Parada do Vez, this two-bedroom house pairs contemporary design with genuine comfort. Both bedrooms have private bathrooms, and the open living space centres on an indoor fireplace and a fully equipped kitchen. Outside, a private pool, garden and barbecue area sit alongside a sauna and hot tub, with air conditioning and a small gym completing the house.

Arcos de Valdevez's historic centre, with its restaurants, cafés and shops, is a few minutes away. The Vez River runs close by, and the wooden Passadiços das Lagoas do Vez walkway, river beaches and trails into Peneda-Gerês National Park are all within easy reach, along with the ancient hilltop site of Citânia de Santa Luzia.

Mornings suit coffee on the patio with the hills still in shadow, then a walk along the river before the day warms. Afternoons might mean the pool or a drive into the national park; evenings call for the sauna and hot tub, then dinner cooked with produce from the local market, eaten by the fire.

Suited to couples or small families wanting quiet and comfort in equal measure, with Portugal Active's local team on hand throughout the stay.

696533616cff760015e28965.tagline: A duplex terrace 300 metres from Cabedelo's surf, with Viana do Castelo close behind.
696533616cff760015e28965.description:
Tide Terrace Duplex spreads three bedrooms and two bathrooms across a bright, split-level layout, sleeping up to six across two queen rooms, a single, and a sofa bed. The living area opens directly onto a private terrace, while a fully equipped kitchen, washer, and private entrance make it easy to settle in for longer stays.

Cabedelo Beach is 300 metres away, a stretch of coast known internationally for windsurfing, kitesurfing and surfing, with the river meeting the ocean nearby. The apartment sits in a quiet residential pocket of Viana do Castelo, close enough to the city centre for cafes and restaurants without the noise of the beach crowds.

Mornings suit breakfast on the terrace, coffee in hand as the light comes off the water. Afternoons mean the short walk down to Cabedelo for a surf lesson or simply watching kitesurfers work the wind, before returning to a quiet garden for the evening.

Well suited to families or groups chasing sea and sport in equal measure, with Portugal Active's concierge on hand throughout the stay.

6965337d2def930014e919c6.tagline: A townhouse in Viana do Castelo, close to sea, station and city streets.
6965337d2def930014e919c6.description:
Urban Reflections spreads over two floors in the heart of Viana do Castelo, with three bedrooms — two doubles and a twin — and three bathrooms for up to six guests. The main suite has its own air conditioning, and the living room opens onto a balcony. A private garage sits alongside free street parking, useful in a town centre setting.

The house sits in a quiet, secure part of the city, an easy walk or short drive from supermarkets, bakeries and local restaurants. Praia do Cabedelo and Praia Norte are minutes away by car, and Monte de Santa Luzia with its funicular is within easy reach. Viana do Castelo train station, roughly ten minutes' drive, connects onward to Porto and Braga.

Mornings suit coffee on the balcony before a walk into town for bread and the market; afternoons can run to the beach or up to Santa Luzia; evenings are for cooking in the well-equipped kitchen and eating at the dining table together.
